# Zumly

> JavaScript library for hierarchical zoom navigation (ZUI). Navigate in Z (depth) through discrete views in the XY plane with spatial transitions.

## What it is

Zumly is a structured, trigger-driven zoom user interface engine. Users zoom into focused elements to open the next view — attention (focus) and depth (Z) stay aligned with layout (XY). It is NOT a freeform pan/zoom canvas or map library.

- Framework-agnostic: works with React, Vue, Svelte, Angular, or plain HTML
- Pluggable transition drivers: CSS, WAAPI, Anime.js, GSAP, Motion, none, or custom
- Plugin system with hash router included
- Touch, keyboard, mouse, and wheel input support

## Key concepts

- **Canvas**: Container element with class `zumly-canvas` where views render
- **View**: A DOM subtree with root class `z-view`. Sources: HTML strings, URLs, async functions, objects with `render()`, web components. Function views get `ctx.target` (the view itself), `props`, `onCleanup`, and `onActivate` (repaint when the view becomes current again)
- **Trigger**: Element with class `zoom-me` and `data-to="viewName"` that initiates zoom-in
- **Depth navigation**: Zoom in/out through view hierarchy (Z axis)
- **Lateral navigation**: Navigate between sibling views at the same depth level. Triggers that share a view and differ in their data (`data-to="room" data-id="kitchen"`) are separate siblings. Each level keeps its own lateral history; `back()` undoes lateral moves before zooming out
- **Driver**: Pluggable animation engine for transitions
- **Plugin**: Object with `install(instance, options)` or plain function
- **Events**: `viewChanged` fires after every navigation with `{ type, viewName, from, zoomLevel, node }`
- **Back button** (`depthNav`): styles `'button'`, `'title'` (title of the view above) or `'rings'` (a ring per level, bands to jump several). Views name themselves with `title` or `data-title`
- **Gestures**: `gestures: { follow: true }` makes trackpad, swipe and pinch (`inputs.pinch`) drive the zoom-out with their progress (`zoomOutProgress` event); `zoomOut(2)` / `zoomOut({ to })` climb several levels in one transition
- **Rasterize**: `rasterize: { snapdom, stream }` shows views behind as a SnapDOM photo, for smooth zooms with heavy views. With SnapDOM's `stream` plugin the photo follows the view, so a zoom starts from what is on screen; a view whose photo would cost too much to keep current, light views and `data-rasterize="false"` stay live. SnapDOM and its plugins are optional peer dependencies
- **WebGL**: `webgl: { snapdom, stream }` (rasterize included) draws zooms in a WebGL canvas and keeps the views behind as textures, with effects in a shader (custom ones in GLSL). `hover: true` prepares a view while the pointer rests on its trigger; `ancestors` (on by default) keeps everything behind past the third level as one picture. For heavy views on weak GPUs.
- **Diagnostics**: the console explains typos in view names and options, and a canvas without size

## Quick start

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://unpkg.com/zumly/dist/zumly.css">
<script src="https://unpkg.com/zumly/dist/zumly.js"></script>
<div style="position: relative; height: 100vh"><!-- the canvas fills this -->
  <div class="zumly-canvas" id="app"></div>
</div>
<script>
  const app = new Zumly({
    mount: '#app',
    initialView: 'home',
    views: {
      home: '<div class="z-view"><div class="zoom-me" data-to="detail">Open</div></div>',
      detail: '<div class="z-view"><p>Detail view</p></div>'
    }
  });
  app.init();
</script>
```

## Ecosystem

- [Orbit](https://zumerlab.com/orbit/) — Radial layouts; satellites work as Zumly triggers. Guide: https://zumerlab.com/zumly/integrations/orbit-css.html
- [SnapDOM](https://github.com/zumerlab/snapdom) — Fast DOM-to-image capture library
